bytes-from-static.title: How Bytes::from_static works
bytes-from-static.description: A Bytes that points at static data: no allocation, no copy.

slides.caption: Cloning it is just copying a pointer and a length.
Use it like a byte slice.
Bytes::from(vec) takes ownership of a Vec.

bytes-copy-from-slice.title: How Bytes::copy_from_slice works
bytes-copy-from-slice.description: A Bytes holding a copy of a slice.

slides.caption: Use it when the source is temporary.
from_static avoids the copy for static data.

bytes-slice.title: How Bytes::slice works
bytes-slice.description: A sub-range of the Bytes that shares the same memory.

slides.caption: Bytes is reference-counted: slices of it point into the same buffer and keep it alive.
A new Bytes over the same memory.
This is why Bytes is popular in network code: cheap sub-slices.

bytes-split-to.title: How Bytes::split_to works
bytes-split-to.description: Removes the first n bytes and returns them as their own Bytes.

slides.caption: Perfect for parsing: cut off a header, keep the body. No bytes are copied.
split_off(n) keeps the front and returns the back.

bytes-split-off.title: How Bytes::split_off works
bytes-split-off.description: Splits at n: self keeps the front, the back is returned.

slides.caption: No copy: both share the buffer.

bytes-truncate.title: How Bytes::truncate works
bytes-truncate.description: Shortens the Bytes to n bytes.

slides.caption: Does nothing if it is already shorter.

bytes-slice-ref.title: How Bytes::slice_ref works
bytes-slice-ref.description: Turns a &[u8] that points into this Bytes into a Bytes, without copying.

slides.caption: Panics if the slice is not inside b.

bytesmut-with-capacity.title: How BytesMut::with_capacity works
bytesmut-with-capacity.description: An empty, growable buffer with room for n bytes.

slides.caption: Writing within the capacity does not reallocate.

bytesmut-extend-from-slice.title: How BytesMut::extend_from_slice works
bytesmut-extend-from-slice.description: Appends bytes, growing the buffer if needed.

bytesmut-freeze.title: How BytesMut::freeze works
bytesmut-freeze.description: Turns the buffer into an immutable, cheaply cloneable Bytes.

slides.caption: Build data in a BytesMut, then freeze it and share it: clones of Bytes are cheap.
Bytes::try_into_mut can go back if it is unique.

bytesmut-split-to.title: How BytesMut::split_to works
bytesmut-split-to.description: Cuts off the first n bytes as their own BytesMut.

slides.caption: The classic way to take one complete message off a read buffer.

bytesmut-split.title: How BytesMut::split works
bytesmut-split.description: Takes everything written so far, leaving an empty buffer with the spare capacity.

slides.caption: buf keeps the remaining capacity for more writes.

bytesmut-reserve.title: How BytesMut::reserve works
bytesmut-reserve.description: Makes sure there is room for n more bytes.

slides.caption: May reclaim space freed by earlier split_to calls.

bytesmut-resize.title: How BytesMut::resize works
bytesmut-resize.description: Sets the length, filling new bytes with a value.

bytesmut-unsplit.title: How BytesMut::unsplit works
bytesmut-unsplit.description: Joins back a BytesMut that was split off, without copying if they are adjacent.

slides.caption: Copies only when the two are not contiguous.

bytesmut-truncate.title: How BytesMut::truncate works
bytesmut-truncate.description: Shortens the buffer, keeping its capacity.

slides.caption: Panics if nothing is left; try_get_u8 returns a Result.
All get_* methods advance the buffer.

buf-get-u16.title: How Buf::get_u16 works
buf-get-u16.description: Reads 2 bytes as a big-endian u16 and advances.

slides.caption: Big-endian means the first byte is the high byte: 0x0102 = 258. get_u16_le reads little-endian.
There are get_u32, get_i64, get_f64... in both byte orders.

buf-get-u32-le.title: How Buf::get_u32_le works
buf-get-u32-le.description: Reads 4 bytes as a little-endian u32.

slides.caption: The first byte is the low byte.
x86 and most file formats use little-endian.

buf-remaining.title: How Buf::remaining works (Bytes)
buf-remaining.description: How many bytes are left to read.

slides.caption: Check it before get_* to avoid panics.
Panics if fewer than n bytes are left.
Use it to skip padding or known headers.

buf-copy-to-bytes.title: How Buf::copy_to_bytes works (Bytes)
buf-copy-to-bytes.description: Takes the next n bytes as a Bytes (zero-copy when the source is Bytes).

slides.caption: For Bytes sources it is just a slice.

buf-chunk.title: How Buf::chunk works (Bytes)
buf-chunk.description: The bytes that can be read right now, as a slice (without advancing).

slides.caption: For chained buffers it may be only the first part.
Then advance() past what you used.

buf-take.title: How Buf::take works
buf-take.description: A view that reads at most n bytes of the buffer.

slides.caption: Useful to hand a sub-parser exactly one field.

bufmut-put-u16.title: How BufMut::put_u16 works
bufmut-put-u16.description: Appends a u16 in big-endian order.

slides.caption: Big-endian writes the high byte first. put_u16_le writes the low byte first.
Panics if a fixed-size buffer has no room.

bufmut-put-f64-le.title: How BufMut::put_f64_le works
bufmut-put-f64-le.description: Appends an f64 as 8 little-endian bytes.

bufmut-put-bytes.title: How BufMut::put_bytes works (Vec)
bufmut-put-bytes.description: Appends one byte value n times.

slides.caption: Faster than a loop of put_u8.

bufmut-remaining-mut.title: How BufMut::remaining_mut works
bufmut-remaining-mut.description: How many more bytes can be written.

slides.caption: Growable buffers report a huge number.

buf-get-i64-le.title: How Buf::get_i64_le works
buf-get-i64-le.description: Reads 8 bytes as a little-endian i64.

buf-has-remaining.title: How Buf::has_remaining works
buf-has-remaining.description: true while there are bytes left to read.

bufmut-put-i32-le.title: How BufMut::put_i32_le works
bufmut-put-i32-le.description: Appends an i32 as 4 little-endian bytes.

bufmut-put-u32.title: How BufMut::put_u32 works
bufmut-put-u32.description: Appends a u32 in big-endian (network) order.

slides.caption: A common way to frame messages: length first, then the bytes.

bytes-try-into-mut.title: How Bytes::try_into_mut works
bytes-try-into-mut.description: Turns a Bytes back into a BytesMut if no one else shares it.

buf-try-get-u16.title: How Buf::try_get_u16 works
buf-try-get-u16.description: Like get_u16, but returns Err instead of panicking when too few bytes are left.

slides.caption: Every get_* has a try_get_* form.
